title: Slotization econ heuristics sketch
body:
Purpose:
This is a quick working sketch of 'slotization' as an operational knob for smoothing microburst costs while bounding tail latency. I want to capture initial heuristics, a lightweight benchmark table, and two simple ASCII charts that product/console folks can riff on. Not a finished analysis — more of a lab notebook/draft to align on next experiments.

Context and motivation:
- We frequently see short, high-concurrency bursts that inflate per-token cost: frequent cold starts, small batches, and short sessions penalize amortization.
- Existing levers (prefill, prewarm, kv-cache) help but are either heavy-handed or increase steady-state cost. Slotization: carve GPU capacity into fixed-duration slots that absorb burst arrivals with predictable amortization.
- Goal: reduce unit cost for short bursts while keeping p95/p99 within acceptable SLO delta (target: +<20% p95 compared to on-demand).

Definitions (working):
- slot: an allocation time window on a GPU instance reserved for a logical session group (e.g., 200ms, 500ms, 1s, tunable).
- slot_size: duration of the slot.
- slot_granularity: number of simultaneous slots (higher granularity = smaller slot durations per GPU).
- smoothing: how slots absorb arrivals vs immediate new allocations (simple: fill slot queue then fall back to on-demand).

Hypothesis:
- Small slot_size (200–500ms) captures most microbursts (short-lived sessions) and yields large amortization gains for token compute and KV cache reuse.
- Too-large slot_size increases queuing latency and tail degradation for sustained interactive workloads.
- There is a convex tradeoff: cost decreases with slot_size up to a point, then plateau; latency penalty increases nonlinearly past a threshold.

Microbench setup (mini):
- Model: open-13B-ish trimmed runtime (optimized kernels), seq_len profile median 128, tail 512.
- Hardware: single A10G-like instance (proxy), isolated bench harness.
- Arrival pattern: spike of 500 short sessions (median 3 turns), then decay; and steady baseline of 50 qps.
- Measures: amortized cost per 1k tokens (USD-equivalent), p50/p95/p99 generation latency, observed KV cache hit-rate (approx).
- Smoothing policy: slots preferred, up to slot_capacity; overflow -> on-demand.

Results (rough, proto numbers — illustrative):
(Columns: slot_size_ms | cost_per_1k_usd | p50_ms | p95_ms | p99_ms | kv_hitrate)
- 0 (on-demand):  | 0.125 | 58 | 260 | 720 | 8%
- 200 ms slots:   | 0.078 | 72 | 320 | 780 | 46%
- 500 ms slots:   | 0.064 | 95 | 410 | 980 | 62%
- 1000 ms slots:  | 0.058 | 150 | 650 | 1600 | 71%

Interpretation notes:
- Cost drops quickly going from on-demand -> 200ms -> 500ms, largely due to reduced per-session startup and better KV reuse (hitrate rise).
- p50 impact modest; p95/p99 grow with slot_size. At 500ms the p95 rise (~+~150ms) might be acceptable for background/low-interactivity APIs but marginal for strict interactive product flows.
- At 1s the p99 is clearly unacceptable for interactive chat; but great for batch/embedding-style workloads where latency SLO is relaxed.

Operational heuristics (first draft):
- Default: 200 ms slot for burst-prone customer tiers (dev/proto, self-serve defaults). Good cost wins, modest latency impact.
- Conservative: 500 ms for background/batch-heavy endpoints (embeddings, rerank where p95 budget higher).
- Interactive-high-sla: disable slotization or use very small slots (<=100ms) combined with warm pools and prefetch.
- Auto-tune candidate: monitor p95 shifting + cost delta; if p95 drift > 15% for >5m, reduce slot_size or move route to a different scheduling tier.
- Hybrid mode: use short slot preference for initial 2 turns of a session (where most bursts hit) then move to on-demand steady path for long conversations.

Open questions / next experiments:
- How does slotization interact with multi-tenant packing and GPU preemption? Need to simulate mixed tenants.
- Can we do adaptive slots: short slots by default but extend a slot (fast path) if reuse is observed in the first X ms? (cheap extension API)
- Explore cost model sensitivity to KV cache eviction policy and sequence length mix (we only used median=128).
- Quantify customer-visible UX: p95 increase may be ok for some flows but not others — need empirical mapping of SLO -> revenue sensitivity.

Suggested next steps:
1) Run cluster-scale sim with realistic tenant mix (use session traces) and confirm cost savings at 95% CI. (owner: Diego)
2) Prototype an adaptive-slot-extension mechanism (owner: Priya) and microbench in the same harness.
3) Wire a console experiment: UI knob in runtime settings to toggle slot_size and show expected cost delta + estimated percentile impact (product/console).
4) Prepare a 1-pager for infra leadership summarizing potential $/1M annual savings for top 20 customers under typical burst profile.

Notes to self: keep this doc rough. If folks like the idea we should capture a clean metrics table with CI bands and embed real trace histograms. Also keep an eye on whether slotization increases variance in downstream metrics like memory pressure per-GPU.

References / artifacts: see linked_artifacts above — PR contains harness code, ENG ticket tracks rollout plan.

End of sketch.

(If you want charts exported as CSV for notebook plotting, tell me which slot sizes and I'll paste.)
